## Status

**Draft v0.2, revised in the field.** Updated 14 September 2026 after the first morning of soil sampling, so that the protocol describes what is actually being done rather than what was planned. Open questions are marked `[?]` inline where they sit, and collected in §11.

::: {.callout-important}

This protocol assumes **snap-trapping**, two trap-nights per group, ~150 individuals, no live recapture, and that **animals are recorded to the small quadrat, not to a corner or trap**. If any of that changes, the spatial design in §2, the soil design in §5.3 and the data capture in §8 need revisiting.

:::

## 1. Purpose and scope

Collect host and paired environmental samples from bank voles (*Clethrionomys glareolus*) at Pallasjärvi, Finnish Lapland, to support WP1 of the Microbial Sensor project: establishing whether structured components of the gut microbiome track host connectivity, using within-campaign spatial co-occurrence as the connectivity proxy. See `data-management-plan.qmd` §2 for how "connected" is operationally defined here, now that this is prospective rather than archived data.

WP1 is Pallasjärvi only: a single prospective field campaign, snap-trapped 12–17 September 2026 on Prof. Heikki Henttonen's (LUKE) existing long-term monitoring design, targeting ~150 individuals. There is no archived-sample component.

Sample types: gut tissue (caecum and distal colon, separately), lung and kidney for PUUV detection, soil at every quadrat corner, field blanks, and off-grid reference soil. Nest material is not obtainable at this site (§5.4).

## 2. Site and trapping design

- Field lead: Prof. Heikki Henttonen (LUKE) and team.
- Site: Pallasjärvi long-term monitoring grids.
- 30 small quadrats (SQ), 15 × 15 m, in groups of 3–7, ≥50 m apart within a group.
- Group membership is **not recorded in the field**. It is derived afterwards from the corner coordinates, by clustering SQ centroids; the within-group spacing (≥50 m) is well inside GPS precision, so the derivation is unambiguous.
- Groups in old forest and in peatland/bog; some peatland groups sit near forest, so voles are caught there too.
- Traps sit at the four corners of each SQ: three snap traps per corner, placed within roughly 3–5 m of the corner marker. Exact trap positions are not recorded.
- Animals are recorded to the SQ only. Henttonen's sample record does not associate an animal with a corner or a trap.
- Traps set day 1; checked day 2; checked and collected day 3.
- **Pitfall lines.** Henttonen's team also runs pitfall lines. Two, `MS` and `MS+` (written "MS extra" on some tubes), were sampled on 14 September. Pitfall animals are recorded to the line only. `[?]` Line length and pitfall spacing are not yet known; infer from the soil-point coordinates and ask Henttonen.

**Spatial resolution.** Because animals are known only to SQ, the host side of the design has three nested scales — SQ, group, habitat. The 15 × 15 m quadrat is the finest scale at which a vole can be placed. Corner resolution exists only on the soil side (§5.3), where it is used to estimate the SQ-level soil signature and its within-quadrat spread, not to place animals.

Corner coordinates come from a consumer handheld GPS, with a per-fix error of roughly 2 m. SQ centroids are therefore good to about 1 m and between-quadrat distances are reliable; within-quadrat distances are not, and the corner is treated as a categorical label with known 15 m and 21 m geometry rather than as a measured position. The forest/peatland contrast provides a within-site environmental contrast.

## 3. Approvals

Biosecurity approval for transporting biological material Uppsala ↔ Finland is handled via the UU biosecurity officer under UU's overarching licence; form drafted and updated 07 Sep 2026. Trapping and animal handling are covered by Henttonen's Finnish permits.

Carry a copy of the approved form with the samples in the car.

## 4. Consumables and equipment

| Item | Purpose | Status |
|---|---|---|
| 2 ml Sarstedt Biosphere plus SafeSeal tubes (PCR performance tested; free of DNA, DNase, RNase and PCR inhibitors) | soil, field blanks, reference soil | in use throughout. Certification is defensive rather than required (Elin), but cheap. Snap cap is fine for dry soil at −20 °C. Rounded base: keep a rack or foam block in the cool bag |
| 10 ml tubes, 100 | were for nest and burrow material | not needed — no nest material is obtainable (§5.4). Spares only |
| 81-place cryoboxes for 2 ml tubes | freezer storage; same format as the gut cryovials | in use |
| Cryovials | gut (transfer in Uppsala) | not needed for the trip; sort out before gut processing |
| 1 dl self-sealing minigrip bags | gut, at dissection | Henttonen provides |
| Disposable wooden waxing spatulas (narrow tip) | clearing litter and loading soil; single use per tube. Not sterile, so keep the box sealed in a ziplock and use one lot for the whole campaign | in use |
| Nitrile gloves | fresh pair per tube | in use |
| Pencil or solvent-proof marker | tube labelling | in use |
| Handheld GPS | one waypoint per corner, named with the sample ID | in use |
| Min/max temperature logger | inside car freezer | in place |
| Frozen gel packs | thermal mass / power-failure buffer | in place |
| Cool bag or coolbox | holds the morning's tubes until transfer to the station freezer | in use |
| Waterproof notebook | field record; transcribed each evening (§8) | in use |

Tubes must be certified DNA-free/DNase-free, not merely sterile — low-biomass samples such as soil are where reagent and plasticware contaminants masquerade as signal.

**Tube count.** 30 SQ × (4 corner soils + 1 field blank) = 150 tubes, plus 8 off-grid reference soils = 158. The first morning covered 10 SQ (50 tubes), so the grid takes about three mornings.

## 5. Sample collection

| Sample | Collected by | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| Lung and kidney for PUUV | Henttonen, existing SOP | Hantavirus surveillance — unchanged from current practice |
| Caecum | Henttonen's team, at dissection | Host gut community; separate sample ID |
| Distal colon | Henttonen's team, at dissection | Host gut community, standardised against WP2 faecal swabs; separate sample ID |
| Soil at every SQ corner | Field team | Environmental channel — SQ-level soil signature and its within-quadrat spread |
| Field blanks, off-grid reference soil | Field team | Contamination check and biological comparator (§5.5) |

Nest and burrow material was planned but is not collectable here (§5.4).

### 5.1 Gut

- Caecum and distal colon in separate bags, one row per animal, two sample IDs.
- Collected by Henttonen at dissection into minigrip bags; frozen the same day. Henttonen dissects every animal, with us assisting, so dissector is constant and not recorded per animal.
- Transfer from bags to cryovials happens in Uppsala, on dry ice (§10).

Record if the caecum tears during dissection; cross-contamination between caecum and colon breaks the comparison between them.

No separate tissue is retained for host genotyping. If the kinship term is funded, host DNA comes from the gut wall: a piece of colon or caecum tissue is cut into its own tube at the cryovial transfer (§10), so the genotyping and microbiome workflows never draw on the same tube.

Vole data are entered by Henttonen's team rather than by us (§8). Their record holds **time of trap check and time of dissection**, so the post-mortem interval covariate is available. **Gut fullness and caecum state** (torn or intact) are recorded at dissection for the animals we sample. On the first morning every colon and caecum seen contained faeces.

### 5.2 PUUV

No blood is taken. Henttonen takes **lung and kidney** from every animal for PUUV detection, under his existing SOP and unchanged from current practice. This protocol points to that SOP rather than duplicating it. The result is joined to our vole table on `animal_id` when it is available.

`[?]` SOP reference or citation, and the detection method (antigen vs. RT-PCR), so the endpoint can be described correctly.

### 5.3 Soil

- **One tube at each of the four corners of every SQ**, whether or not a vole was caught there. 120 soils in total.
- Taken from the nearest **runway or burrow opening** to the corner marker, i.e. from substrate the animals actually use, rather than from an arbitrary point at the corner. Runway and burrow opening are not distinguished in the record: at a fixed horizon, and with no information on whether the feature is active, the distinction is an uncontrolled covariate that would not be analysed.
- Sampling horizon: **2 cm below the litter and needle layer**, standardised across all points.
- Fill the 2 ml tube to about two-thirds — roughly 0.5–1.5 g depending on how loose the organic layer is. That is two to five extractions' worth, which leaves room for re-extraction. Leave headroom for freeze expansion.
- Clear the litter with the spatula, then load with the spatula or scoop directly with the tube mouth. Nothing that has touched litter goes into the tube.
- **Fresh spatula and fresh gloves for every tube.**
- **One GPS waypoint per corner**, named with the sample ID (§7).
- One tube per corner. Do not take duplicates as routine; a second tube means a second sample ID and is almost never processed.

Why every corner rather than only capture points: the animal's corner is unknown, so the quantity that pairs with a host is the SQ-level soil signature. Four corners per SQ estimate that signature, and the five fully-sequenced SQs in §5.6 estimate how much it varies within a quadrat. Sampling only the corners with captures would give no more host resolution and a worse SQ estimate.

**Pitfall lines.** Two soils per line plus one field blank, same tube, horizon and hygiene as the corner soils, one waypoint per soil. A line is a longer and differently shaped unit than a 15 × 15 m quadrat, is trapped by a different method, and gets half the soil coverage, so pitfall soils and pitfall voles are held as their own stratum in the data (§8) and are not counted among the 120 quadrat soils. Whether pitfall voles can enter the dyadic connectivity model is an open scientific question (§11); the samples are collected so that the option exists.

### 5.4 Nest and burrow material

**Not collected.** Burrows at this site are deep, and nest material cannot be reached without excavation. The runway and burrow-opening soil collected under §5.3 is the closest available proxy for shared burrow infrastructure.

If nest material is encountered opportunistically (e.g. a nest exposed at the surface), it goes into a 10 ml tube or a minigrip bag with the SQ number and material type, but this is not expected.

### 5.5 Controls collected alongside real samples

- **Field blanks** — an empty tube of the same type, opened at a sampling point, left open for roughly the time a real sample takes, closed, and then handled identically to real samples all the way through extraction and sequencing. These catch airborne and handling contamination. **One per SQ** (30 total), which is a denser series than the one-per-group-per-day originally planned and lets a contaminated quadrat be identified rather than a contaminated day. **The blank is always opened at corner A**, so the corner need not be recorded per tube. Pitfall lines get one blank per line.
- **Off-grid reference soil** — background regional soil signature, collected away from any grid or burrow: four off-grid forest and four off-grid peatland (8 total), same horizon and tube as §5.3. This is a biological comparator, not a contamination check. `[?]` Not yet collected; schedule for a later morning.

Kit blanks, PCR no-template controls, and the mock community standard are lab-stage controls, not field-collected — see `pilot-lab-protocol.qmd`.

### 5.6 Processing subset (soil)

Collect all 120 soils and 30 blanks; extract and sequence ~58 soils plus a subset of blanks:

- **One soil per SQ (30).** `[?]` The rule for choosing it is not yet decided: a randomly drawn corner, a fixed corner, or an equal-mass pool of the four corners at extraction. Pooling gives the best SQ-level estimate but removes the SQ from the within-quadrat comparison below, so the choice interacts with the next item.
- **All four corners in 5 SQs (20).** This estimates the **within-quadrat variance component**. Because hosts are resolved to SQ, the question it answers is how much information the host–soil pairing loses by being at SQ level rather than corner level — not whether capture-point distance matters, which is unmeasurable here. Choose SQs with captures, balanced across forest and peatland.
- **Four off-grid forest + four off-grid peatland reference soils (8).**
- **Field blanks.** `[?]` How many of the 30 to sequence; at minimum one per extraction batch, drawn from the SQs in that batch.

Balance the whole set across forest and peatland.

## 6. Field hygiene

- Sterile or single-use dissection tools per individual for gut sampling. Shared tools across a necropsy series will homogenise the community signal across individuals in a way that is very hard to detect after the fact.
- Fresh spatula and fresh gloves for every soil tube and blank.

## 7. Labelling

- Sample ID is the **SQ number followed by the corner letter**, e.g. `31A`, written on the tube with a solvent-proof marker at the point of collection. Each corner is sampled once, so this is unique across the campaign.
- The GPS waypoint at that corner carries the same string.
- Field blanks: the **SQ number alone**, e.g. `31`. Soils always carry a corner letter, so a bare number is unambiguous. First-morning blanks were written as the SQ number plus "control"; they map to the same ID and are not relabelled.
- Pitfall lines: line name plus running number for soils, line name alone for the blank, following the quadrat convention. In the data: `MS1`, `MS2`, blank `MS`; `MS+1`, `MS+2`, blank `MS+`. Tubes are written with a space ("MS 1", "MS+ 2", "MS (blank)") and some read "MS extra" for `MS+`; these all map to the IDs above.
- Reference soils: proposed `REF-F1`…`REF-F4` and `REF-P1`…`REF-P4`.
- In the data, `sample_id` is the tube label verbatim. A project prefix (`PAL-`) is added only at the point where WP1 and WP2 data are merged, not on tubes.

## 8. Data capture

**KoBo is not used.** The forms in `data-capture/` were built for a design in which each sample carried several per-sample fields worth capturing at the moment of collection. With every corner sampled at a fixed depth into a fixed tube, the per-sample information collapses to the tube label and the GPS waypoint, both of which are recorded outside KoBo anyway. The forms are kept in the repository as a record and are superseded by the two tables below.

**Three tables, transcribed each evening** from the tube labels, the GPS unit and the notebook. Templates with the column headers are in `data-capture/`; the filled files live in `data-raw/wp1_finland/`.

**Soil log** (`wp1_soil_log`), one row per tube — soils, blanks and reference soils:

| Column | Content |
|---|---|
| `sample_id` | tube label (§7): `31A` for soil, `31` for the blank |
| `sample_type` | `soil` / `field_blank` / `reference` |
| `collection_date` | ISO date |
| `sq_id` | SQ number; blank for pitfall and reference soils |
| `line_id` | pitfall line (`MS`, `MS+`); blank for quadrat and reference soils |
| `corner` | A/B/C/D; A for quadrat field blanks; blank for pitfall and reference soils |
| `habitat` | `old_forest` / `peatland` |
| `depth_cm` | 2 unless deviated |
| `collector_initials` | |
| `notes` | |

**Coordinates** (`wp1_corner_coords`), one row per soil point: quadrat corners and pitfall soil points, from the GPS waypoint. Coordinates live here only, keyed by `sq_id` + `corner` or by `line_id` + waypoint, and are joined to the soil log rather than typed into it:

| Column | Content |
|---|---|
| `waypoint_name` | name as stored on the GPS, normally the sample ID (`31A`, `MS1`) |
| `sq_id`, `line_id`, `corner` | as in the soil log |
| `lat`, `lon` | WGS84 decimal degrees, at least five decimal places |
| `collection_date` | |
| `notes` | |

`R/03_wp1_soil_point_coords.R` loads this file, applies a documented corrections table (the raw file is never edited), imputes a missing fourth corner where three were recorded, and writes the point, quadrat and pitfall-line tables to `data/field_sites/`. Entry errors found by that script are corrected in its table, not in the raw file. If the GPS unit exports GPX, the export goes into `data-raw/wp1_finland/sampling/` and `R/01_wp1_trap_grid_gpx.R` builds the same tables with no transcription.

**Vole table** (`wp1_voles`), one row per animal. Henttonen will share his own Excel sheet rather than have us transcribe the lab notes, so his sheet is the primary record: it is stored unaltered in `data-raw/wp1_finland/` and its columns are mapped to the ones below by script, not retyped. The columns marked "ours" are the only ones we fill by hand, keyed on `animal_id`. The full column list is kept as the target schema so the mapping has something fixed to land on:

| Column | Content | Source |
|---|---|---|
| `processing_date` | date of necropsy | lab notes |
| `animal_id` | Henttonen's ID — the join to his morphometrics and the PUUV result, which arrives later and is joined on this column, not copied here | lab notes |
| `capture_date` | date the trap was checked; usually equals `processing_date` | lab notes |
| `sq_id`, `line_id`, `habitat` | as in the soil log; exactly one of `sq_id` and `line_id` is filled | lab notes |
| `trap_check_time`, `necropsy_time` | the difference is the post-mortem interval | lab notes |
| `species`, `sex` | | lab notes |
| `head_body_mm`, `tail_mm`, `mass_g` | | lab notes |
| `age_class` | as Henttonen's team classes it (e.g. juvenile / subadult / adult, or overwintered vs. young of the year) | lab notes |
| `repro_status` | males: testes scrotal / abdominal; females: perforate, pregnant, lactating, placental scars — as recorded | lab notes |
| `embryos_n` | if pregnant | lab notes |
| `carcass_condition` | fresh / autolysed / scavenged / wet, and whether the animal was alive at the check (pitfalls) | lab notes or ours |
| `wounds` | bite wounds or scars, yes / no with a note | lab notes or ours |
| `caecum_sample_id`, `colon_sample_id` | | ours |
| `gut_fullness`, `caecum_torn` | full / partial / empty; yes / no (§5.1) | ours |
| `notes` | | |

Not recorded per animal because they are constant: the dissector (Henttonen, throughout), PUUV tissue (lung and kidney, every animal, §5.2), and tissue for host genotyping (the gut samples themselves, §10).

**The location join is not in Henttonen's sheet.** His animal ID is the same as written on the gut bags, but the quadrat or line an animal came from exists only in his field notebook. So each evening, while the notebook is to hand, record for every animal we sample: `animal_id`, `sq_id` or `line_id`, `caecum_sample_id`, `colon_sample_id`, `gut_fullness` and `caecum_torn`. The first two are the join between host and soil and cannot be reconstructed from Uppsala. Everything else comes from his sheet; columns his sheet does not carry are left blank, not guessed.

The join between the two tables is `sq_id` for quadrat animals and `line_id` for pitfall animals, never corner: a vole pairs with all soils of its unit. Group is attached to both tables afterwards from the derived SQ-to-group lookup (§2). Sample IDs follow §7; `data-management-plan.qmd` §3 points here.

## 9. Cold chain

- Samples go to the **field station freezer** during the day. Confirmed working on the first morning.
- Transfer to the **car freezer** (compressor, −18/−20 °C, 18 L) in one batch in the evening. Batch the loading: one door opening per day, not thirty. The car freezer runs on mains at the station, with the logger and gel packs in place.
- The morning's tubes sit in a cool bag while working.
- **Frozen gel packs** in the freezer for thermal mass — this is the real buffer against a power interruption.
- **Min/max logger inside the freezer.**
- Freezer on 12 V while driving, on mains at the station and at overnight stops. Bring the mains adapter.
- No preservative. Samples are stored dry and frozen. This is only defensible while the cold chain holds — hence the logger.

## 10. On arrival in Uppsala

- Transfer gut from minigrip bags to cryovials on dry ice, without thawing. At the same step, if host genotyping is going ahead, cut a piece of gut wall from each animal into a separate labelled tube (§5.1).
- Move everything to institutional −20 °C at IEG. Freezer space is confirmed and −20 °C agreed as adequate for soil and gut (Elin, 09 Sep 2026). The gut transfer to cryovials can be scheduled later, before processing.

**To resolve during the campaign (unrecoverable afterwards):**

- Off-grid reference soils, 4 forest + 4 peatland, still to collect (§5.5).
- Obtain Henttonen's Excel sheet before leaving. Animal ID matches the gut bags (confirmed 14 Sep); the sampling unit does not appear in the sheet and must be taken from his notebook animal by animal, each evening (§8).
- Pitfall line length and spacing, from Henttonen (§2).

**To resolve before processing:**

- The one-soil-per-SQ rule: random corner, fixed corner, or pooled (§5.6).
- Number of field blanks to sequence (§5.6).
- Derive the SQ-to-group lookup from the corner coordinates once all SQs are sampled (§2).
- PUUV SOP reference and detection method (§5.2).
- Biosafety/PPE reference for handling wild-rodent carcasses and excreta — likely already covered by Henttonen's existing PUUV field SOP; link it here rather than duplicate.
- The operational connectivity definition in `data-management-plan.qmd` §2 must be at SQ level or coarser, since co-capture at a trap or corner is not observable.
- **Pitfall lines.** Line length and pitfall spacing (infer from coordinates; ask Henttonen). Whether the ~6 pitfall voles enter the dyadic connectivity model at all: co-capture on a line is a weaker and differently shaped co-occurrence than co-capture in a 15 × 15 m quadrat, and there is no within-line resolution. Options are a unit-type term with unit extent as a covariate, or excluding pitfall voles from the dyadic model and using them only for the host–soil channel. This is a modelling decision, not a field one.

:::
